## Variables

### DBH

```{r}
# Diamteter at breast height
summary(forestry.all$DBH)
```

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 100 & DBH > 0) |> pull(DBH),main = "DBH Histogram", xlab = "Diameter at Breast Height", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 100 & DBH > 0) |> pull(DBH),main = "DBH Boxplot", ylab = "Diameter at Breast Height", col = "gray60")
```

```{r}
forestry.all |> filter(DBH < 0)
```

```{r}
forestry.all |> filter(DBH > 100) |> select(SCI_NM, DBH)
```

### MBG Width

```{r}
# MBG - The horizontal measurement of a tree's foliage and branches, usually defined as the average distance between the outermost driplines on opposite sides of the tree. It serves as a key indicator of tree vigor, competitive capacity, and canopy closure in forestry and ecological studies. Measurements are in feet and were derived from 2020 lidar data.

par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_WIDTH),main = "MBG Width Histogram", xlab = "Horizontal Measure of Foliage and Branches", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_WIDTH),main = "MBG Width Boxplot", ylab = "Horizontal Measure of Foliage and Branches", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

### MBG Length

```{r}
# The vertical measurement of a tree from the top (highest live foliage) down to the base of the live crown, typically defined as the lowest, non-epicormic, live branch. It represents the active, photosynthetic portion of the tree, indicating its health, vigor, and capacity for growth. Measurements are in feet and were derived from 2020 lidar data.

par(mfrow=c(1,2), bg = "gray40")
hist(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_LENGTH),main = "MBG Length Histogram", xlab = "Vertical Measure from top to live crown", col = "gray60")
boxplot(forestry.all |> pull(MBG_LENGTH),main = "MBG Length Boxplot", ylab = "Vertical Measure from top to live crown", pch = "+", col = "gray60")
```

## Appendix

### RETIREDDT

This variable basically informs us that there are two separate data sets we should work with. The living trees, and the dead ones.

Only 5452 trees are alive. The rest have been "retired".

```{r}
livetrees <- forestry.all |> filter(RETIREDDT != "NA")
nrow(livetrees)
```

## Potential Variables of interest

Could measure CONDITION (categorical variable) with the numerical predictors of DBH, TBOX_L, TBOX_W, MBG_WIDTH\*, and MAX_CROWN_HEIGHT.

Potential logistic regression, where we split condition into "good" or "bad," and then we can estimate the probability of a tree being that way.

```{r}
y <- "CONDITION"
num_vars <- c("DBH", "TBOX_L", "TBOX_W", "MBG_WIDTH", "MAX_CROWN_HEIGHT")
cat_vars <- c("GENUS_NAME", "WARD", "WIRES", "CURB", "SIDEWALK")

# where are NAs

forestry.all |> 
  select(all_of(c(y, num_vars, cat_vars))) |> 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ round(100 * mean(is.na(.x) | .x == ""), 1))) |> 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "pct_missing") |> 
  arrange(desc(pct_missing)) |> 
  print()

# potential predictors (numericals)
summary(forestry.all[num_vars])

forestry.all |> 
  select(all_of(num_vars)) |> 
  pivot_longer(everything()) |> 
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal()

# collinearity check
cor_mat <- cor(forestry.all[num_vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
round(cor_mat, 2)
heatmap(cor_mat, symm = TRUE)

# There's some concern with the MBG_WIDTH, but not about .6 on the correlation matrix with any other variables.
```
